scope: SANDBOX task scheduling; no strategy or risk changes

root_cause.problem: High-churn task leases and completions shared a historical table and a partial due index. Vacuum thresholds scaled with retained history; the small live queue could require a large physical index scan.
root_cause.previous_repair: SIGNAL_QUEUE_INDEX_REPAIR_20261110.json describes the earlier concurrent reindex and immediate vacuum mitigation. This change separates the unfinished task projection from retained history.

architecture.canonical: v2_strategy_tasks remains authoritative for identity, attempts, leases, deadlines and completion; historical decisions and financial records are unchanged.
architecture.ready: v2_strategy_ready contains unfinished (consumer,signal_id) keys only. AFTER INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE ALWAYS trigger synchronizes it in the same transaction.
architecture.lease_churn: Lease/retry updates probe membership but do not rewrite an existing ready row.
architecture.claim: Materialized ready keys, read-only primary-key candidate probes, then original task recheck and single-row FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED. No scan of the historical due index in the tested claim plan.
architecture.concurrency: Original task leases remain shared by old and new workers; rollback, abandoned-lease recovery and single selected-row locking are tested.
architecture.fallback: Missing/disabled/unvalidated projection or failed advisory gate uses the canonical task query, not an empty queue. Actual claim/ACK errors are not swallowed.
architecture.migration: Every DDL run invalidates prior validation. Trigger starts before bounded backfill; skipped locked tasks are revisited. Only exact bidirectional set validation under short locks enables READY.

online_schema.operator: scripts/v2_ready_queue_migrate_20261110.py; dry-run unless --execute; fixed sandbox database identity and original task owner required

production_scale_read_only_plan.limit: Timing is a SELECT analogue with row locking and UPDATE removed, not live claim latency, physical disk I/O or a matched before/after benchmark.

monitor.notification: Existing DM-only host health transitions; durable delivery acknowledgement and dedup. Unknown preserves previous alarms.
checks: correct always-enabled sync trigger and validated control

monitor.claim_p95: NOT_PROVIDED; aggregate claim_ms/processed is not a P95
monitor.writes: Diagnostic snapshot and notification acknowledgement only; no repair, reindex, task rewrite or order authority

regressions_caught_and_fixed: Locking a LATERAL subquery alias locked all ready candidates rather than only the selected task.
A plain JOIN could still choose the historical partial due index. Two-stage primary-key lookups and canonical state rechecks now prevent that tested plan.
Repeat migration could preserve a stale enabled marker after a disabled trigger missed tasks. Each migration now invalidates proof before restoring the trigger.
qa.harness_correction: Initial monitor artifact QA lacked the new migration fixture file; copied only the test DDL into the isolated harness and reran all 94 cases successfully. No runtime code was changed for this correction.
coverage: transaction rollback and original task fields/xmin/ctid preservation during migration

same-count different-member projection mismatch, bounded backfill skip-and-revisit

controller_release.condition: Fresh local and exchange flat proof before and after graceful stop; same account binding and unchanged risk policy. Existing flat-only authorization is preserved.

final_runtime_check.interpretation: Background history maintenance reported degradation again; it did not block these cycles. Do not label the entire system problem-free.

release_verification_20261111.protection_exit_settlement_checks: CLEAR in all six observed cycles; these are management checks, not new fill evidence
release_verification_20261111.independent_review: Exact four-file manifest and flat-only same-binding release protocol reviewed; no blocking findings

limitations: The new claim path became active on 2026-11-11. Six initial completed cycles verify runtime use, not a multi-day latency guarantee or a new open-close round trip.
The ready queue grows with genuinely unfinished tasks; it is not an absolute backlog cap. Existing bounded expiry maintenance and lag monitoring remain necessary.
Fixed vacuum triggers are maintenance requests, not a guarantee against long transactions, I/O saturation or stalled autovacuum. Independent monitoring remains necessary.
No multi-day recurrence-free claim or profitability claim is made. Observe churn and real claim latency after cutover.
Earlier background history timeouts and an unclassified CONTEXT ValueError are not claimed fixed by this work.
Original SQL due index is retained for canonical fallback and bounded unfinished-task checks. The new hot claim avoids it; historical storage is not removed.
